CAROLYN BOURDEAUX.ideology: GPB (May 2022) described her as more moderate than some Democrats, a member of the Problem Solvers Caucus and the Blue Dog Coalition, criticized by progressive activists, and representing a different wing of the party from Lucy McBath; Wikipedia's reference list also places her in the New Democrat Coalition. FiveThirtyEight scored her as voting with President Biden's stated position 100% of the time as of Aug. 2021. OnTheIssues' VoteMatch labels her a 'Populist-Leaning Liberal'. In Aug. 2021 she was one of nine House Democrats who told Speaker Pelosi they 'will not consider voting for a budget resolution' until the bipartisan infrastructure bill became law. She said in 2022: 'I ground everything in the needs of the people of this district.'
CAROLYN BOURDEAUX.record: One term in the U.S. House (117th Congress). Member of the Problem Solvers Caucus, Blue Dog Coalition and New Democrat Coalition. On Aug. 12, 2021 she and eight other House Democrats wrote Speaker Pelosi that they 'will not consider voting for a budget resolution' until the bipartisan infrastructure bill was signed into law; she later voted for the $3.5 trillion budget resolution, voted Yea on the $1.2 trillion infrastructure bill (Nov. 5, 2021) and Yea on passage of the Build Back Better Act (Nov. 19, 2021). In the 2022 primary she defended her role in slowing Build Back Better and touted work on Medicaid expansion and studying reparations. Before Congress she directed the Georgia Senate Budget and Evaluation Office (2007-2010) during the recession-era budget cuts and taught public policy at Georgia State.

orig.background: William C. Gaulden Jr., of Athens. Works in the funeral industry (Winfery Mutual Funeral Home) and attended Gupton-Jones College of Funeral Service, working toward licensure as a funeral director and embalmer; formerly head of candidate relations at the Clarke County School District and owner of W. Gaulden Enterprise, Inc. (Branch; Red & Black). Vice chair of the Athens-Clarke County Democratic Party (WUGA; Red & Black). Ran for Athens-Clarke County coroner in 2024 and lost to Michael Eberhart (Red & Black). Announced for the open State Senate District 46 seat (vacated by Republican Bill Cowsert's run for attorney general) in July 2025; lost the May 19, 2026 Democratic primary to Ray Smith with 5,817 votes (40.1%).
